metadata.chapter_subtitle: Why the sensor does not see the surface alone

inventory.summary: The series needed a beginner-safe bridge between raw sensor measurements and physically meaningful surface information, especially before vegetation-index and advanced optical chapters.
issues: Readers needed an explanation of why the atmosphere changes the signal recorded by a sensor.
The difference between top-of-atmosphere measurement and surface reflectance was not yet introduced in the core sequence.
A simple atmospheric-correction concept was needed before more advanced remote-sensing modelling.

rewrite.summary: Added a new foundations chapter that explains scattering, absorption, and surface reflectance in plain language, then ties those ideas to why corrected imagery is better for comparison and modelling.
editor_notes: Used a signal-path narrative so readers can follow energy from Sun to surface to sensor.
Avoided overloading the chapter with full radiative-transfer formalism.
Positioned atmospheric correction as a practical modelling step rather than a specialist detour.

qa_review.summary: The chapter gives a fair introduction to atmospheric effects without overshooting the core-book difficulty target and prepares readers well for later imagery work.

repair.summary: The remote-sensing ladder was repaired by adding a chapter that turns raw-signal questions into a readable explanation of corrected surface information.
actions_taken: Added a chapter on atmospheric effects and surface reflectance to the foundations sequence.
Connected the chapter to downstream work on imagery interpretation and vegetation indices.
Explained the purpose of correction steps in task-focused language.

design_review.summary: The chapter uses a simple signal-path visualization and explanatory framing well, which helps readers picture where distortion enters the measurement chain.
improvements_made: Added a signal-path visual showing how atmosphere and surface both shape what the sensor receives.
Used interpretive guidance to explain what the figure means physically.
Framed surface reflectance as a cleaner modelling input rather than an abstract processing product.
